figures.caption: Coefficient of determination between recovered (classifier-filtered salmon) and simulated L1 abundance at three aggregation levels — per-locus, per-subfamily, and total — showing recovery is identifiable at the aggregate level while individual near-identical loci are not.
figures.description: Bar chart of pooled R-squared at per-locus, per-subfamily, and total aggregation. The rise with aggregation is the central result: short reads cannot resolve >99% identical young L1 to a single locus, but the model recovers L1 abundance exactly at the family level.

figures.caption: Total (family-level) recovered L1 abundance against the simulated total per grid cell, with the linear fit and coefficient of determination.
figures.description: Per-cell scatter of recovered total salmon NumReads against simulated total transcript copies across all insertion-level by deletion-probability cells, annotated with the total-level R-squared.

figures.caption: Mean recovered total L1 abundance as a function of the simulated expression level from 2^5 to 2^13, tracking the expression gradient across roughly 2.5 orders of magnitude.
figures.description: Log-log line of mean recovered total salmon NumReads per insertion level, showing the classifier-filter to salmon pipeline tracks the simulated L1 expression gradient monotonically.
